title: Platform systems & services — Runbooks, Dashboards, Alerts, Q2 2026 Roadmap & Retro
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the platform systems & services runbooks, dashboard and alert definitions, Q2 2026 roadmap highlights, and the post-Q2 retrospective action items for the Platform team. It is intended as the single-source-of-truth for day-to-day operations and short-term roadmap priorities.

Purpose and audience
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-recover for platform incidents, centralize dashboards/alerts, and align roadmap priorities with operational debt discovered during Q2 2026.
- Audience: Platform on-call, SRE, infra, and platform product managers.

Scope
- Services covered: api-gateway, request-router, batch-orchestrator, kv-cache, model-proxy, metrics-ingest, alert-evaluator.
- Excluded: customer-specific private deployments (see eng-private-deployments reference pages).

Ownership and contacts
- Platform oncall rotation: platform-oncall@redwood.com
- Pager owner (primary): Carlos Ramirez (pager: +1-415-555-0182)
- Secondary escalation: Sophie Nguyen (pager: +1-415-555-0174)
- Platform runbook owner (doc owner): Aisha Patel

Key SLOs and thresholds
- api-gateway: 99.9% availability monthly; P95 latency < 120ms for 1–1024 token requests.
- request-router: 99.95% request routing success; error rate < 0.1% per minute.
- kv-cache: cache hit rate > 75% on average per model-serving tier; stale eviction < 0.5%/hour.
- metrics-ingest: 99.9% of time series written within 15s of event.
- alert-evaluator: rule evaluation latency < 5s per 1k rules.

Dashboards (canonical panels and owners)
- Platform Overview (owner: monitoring@eng-platform) — single-pane summary for oncall:
  - Total request rate (rps) — 1m/5m/15m
  - Error rate (5xx) by service (stacked)
  - End-to-end P95 latency for inference APIs
  - Total running GPUs and queue length for batch jobs
  - KV cache hit rate (service-level)
- api-gateway — owner: infra-team
  - Active connections, SSL handshake failures, request queue depth
  - P95/P99 latencies by route
- model-proxy — owner: serving-runtime
  - Model load time, KV cache miss latency, context window usage distribution
- metrics-ingest / alert-evaluator — owner: platform-observability
  - Write latency histogram, dropped metric count, rule eval errors

Dashboard panel guidance (recommended thresholds)
- Error rate panel: trigger a warning annotation at 0.05% and an urgent alert at 0.1% sustained for 2 minutes.
- P95 latency panel: warning at 200ms, urgent at 400ms sustained for 5 minutes.
- Cache hit rate: warning at 65% sustained for 10 minutes, urgent at 50% sustained for 5 minutes.

Saved queries and dashboards (example Grafana JSON snippet)
- Use the following as a template for panels (replace data source and metric name):

```json
{
  "dashboard": {
    "title": "Platform Overview - template",
    "panels": [
      {"title": "Total RPS", "datasource": "prometheus", "expr": "sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))"},
      {"title": "P95 Latency (api-gateway)", "expr": "histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))"}
    ]
  }
}
```

Alerting rules (prometheus-alertmanager)
- Rule: PlatformHighErrorRate
  - expr: sum by (service) (rate(http_requests_total{status=~\"5..\"}[1m])) / sum by (service) (rate(http_requests_total[1m])) > 0.001
  - for: 2m
  - labels: severity=high, team=platform
  - annotations: runbook_url=/confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-runbook-roadmap-retro-2026-q2

- Rule: KVCacheLowHitRate
  - expr: avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_ratio[10m]) < 0.65
  - for: 10m
  - labels: severity=critical, owner=serving-runtime

Incident runbooks (primary playbooks)
1) High 5xx error rate (api-gateway or request-router)
   1. Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty within 2 minutes.
   2. Check Platform Overview dashboard -> Errors by service -> identify service with spike.
   3. If api-gateway: check recent config deploys (CI/CD) — run `cictl deployment history --service api-gateway --last 3` and rollback to previous stable if a failed deploy correlated with spike.
   4. If request-router: inspect routing table health: `rqctl routes list --format=json | jq '.[] | select(.healthy==false)'`. If unhealthy routes > 0, trigger router-restart play (step 6).
   5. For both: capture request traces via tracing UI (link pinned on dashboard) for a 5 minute window and paste critical trace IDs to the incident ticket.
   6. Router restart play (when safe): follow the rolling restart runbook — restart up to 20% of instances at a time, confirm metrics stabilize for 3 minutes between batches. Owner: infra ops.
   7. Post-incident: file postmortem within 48 hours and tag related deploys/config changes.

2) KV cache degradation
   1. Confirm alert and check cache hit-rate heatmap by model and region.
   2. If degradation isolated to a node pool: cordon node(s) and run `kvctl repair --node <node-id>` (documented in runbooks).
   3. If global: check redis/rocksdb metrics, disk pressure, GC pause times. Escalate to serving-runtime lead if disk/IO issues found.
   4. If KV cache backend (redis) is overloaded: scale the Redis cluster by +1 shard and run rolling reshard (follow oncall playbook).

3) Metrics ingest backlog
   1. Identify backlog size via metrics-ingest queue length panel.
   2. If queue > 10k events and trending up: increase ingestion workers by 25% using autoscaler override: `kubectl -n metrics set hpa metrics-ingest --min=3 --max=20 --cpu-percent=60` or use the internal autoscale dashboard toggle.
   3. If scaling fails, divert noncritical telemetry (debug logs) with service-level flags.

Escalation matrix
- Pager (P0/P1): platform-oncall -> primary pager -> secondary pager -> on-call manager (Ethan Moore) -> VP Platform (exec oncall).
- Slack channel for incident comms: #platform-incident (create private thread for sensitive incidents).

Runbook hygiene and playbook updates
- Each oncall must: verify runbook steps at least once per quarter by performing the dry-run checklist.
- Owners must update runbooks within 7 business days after a related incident or rolling change.

Retrospective summary (Q2 2026)
- Observations:
  - Regressions in cache hit rate correlated with the April model-catalog rollout (model-proxy change).
  - Two incidents caused by misconfigured autoscale policies during a sudden traffic spike in May.
  - Monitoring gap: no single summary panel for model-variant rollout health.
- Impact: total of 9 hours of partial degradation across two incidents; customer-visible latency spikes for mid-tier customers.
- Root causes:
  - Insufficient canary thresholds for model-proxy (canary traffic too low).
  - Autoscaler thresholds tuned for CPU but not request backlog.
- Action items (owners and ETA):
  1. Update model-proxy rollout canary policy to 10% traffic for 15 minutes and add explicit rollback threshold (owner: serving-runtime, ETA: 2026-07-01).
  2. Add a "rollout health" dashboard for model variants and integrate with alert-evaluator (owner: platform-observability, ETA: 2026-06-30).
  3. Rework autoscale policy templates to consider queue length and request latency (owner: eng-infra, ETA: 2026-07-15).
  4. Run a simulated traffic game-day focused on autoscaling behaviors (owner: eng-sre, ETA: 2026-07-20).

Q2 2026 Roadmap highlights (milestones and owners)
- Week of 2026-06-21: Deploy rollout-health dashboard and alert integration (platform-observability).
- July 2026: Autoscaler policy rollout and HPA templates updated across staging and production (eng-infra).
- August 2026: Model-proxy canary policy update and canary tooling improvements (serving-runtime + eng-platform).
- Sep 2026: Comprehensive runbook consolidation and rewrites (platform team-wide initiative).

Dependencies and risks
- Dependency: metrics-ingest scaling relies on cloud provider quotas for ingestion workers. Monitoring for quota usage is pre-configured in cloud-accounts-and-networking pages.
- Risk: aggressive autoscaling changes can cause oscillation if not tested in game-day. We will gate production rollouts behind a successful game-day.

Operational checklists (quick reference)
- Daily (oncall start): check Platform Overview dashboard, ensure alerts queue is clear, verify leader health for critical services.
- Weekly: run `cictl check-configs --stale` and address any pending failed deploys.
- Monthly: update SLO attainment report and notify product teams if any SLOs < 99.9%.

How-tos & runbook snippets
- Rolling restart for request-router (safe windows):
  1. Identify candidate pods: `kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=request-router -o wide`.
  2. Drain one pod: `kubectl -n platform delete pod <pod-name> --grace-period=30` (monitor traffic shift).
  3. Wait until P95 latency returns to baseline for 3 minutes.
  4. Repeat for the next 20% of pods.

- Inspecting traces for slow requests:
  1. Use tracing UI (link on dashboard) and filter by trace.service=request-router and duration>500ms.
  2. Export trace IDs and attach to incident ticket.

- Updating Grafana dashboards safely:
  1. Create dashboard in the staging Grafana folder and validate panels against staging metrics for 48 hours.
  2. Create a PR with dashboard JSON and reference the related page ID.
  3. After approval, promote to production during low-traffic window.

Knowledge base / team wiki links

Appendix: runbook checklist template (to paste in incident ticket)
- Incident summary: [summary]
- First detection time: [timestamp]
- Alert name and query: [alert]
- Actions taken (timestamps):
  - Acknowledged: [time]
  - Triage: [time, finding]
  - Mitigation: [time, steps]
  - Resolution: [time]
- Postmortem owner and ETA: [name, date]

Document maintenance
- This page is owned by: eng-platform.
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any P0 incident.
- Change log: last major update 2026-06-18 (added rollout-health dashboard and KVCache alert tuning).
